 18 Nov 2026, 21:46 UTC · Source: Orlando City SC In 30 seconds Orlando City host FC Cincinnati in the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs Wild Card match on Thursday.
 Orlando went 10W-4L-3D at home in the regular season and beat New England on Decision Day.
 Maxime Crépeau recorded his fifth shutout of the 2026 MLS season in the regular-season finale.
 Orlando City will host FC Cincinnati at Inter.co Stadium on Thursday night in the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs Wild Card match. Orlando City took the No. 8 seed in the Eastern Conference on Decision Day, while Cincinnati finished at No. 9. The winner moves on to Round One, and the loser's season ends.
 Orlando City's home form has been a strength in 2026. The Lions finished the regular season with a 10W-4L-3D record at home after beating the New England Revolution on Decision Day. Thursday's match is Orlando's first home playoff game since 2024, and the club has reached the postseason in seven consecutive seasons.

 Download on the App Store Get it on Google Play Goalkeeper Maxime Crépeau enters the playoffs after recording his fifth shutout of the 2026 MLS campaign in the regular-season finale, a result that helped Orlando City secure the victory and the home-field advantage for the Wild Card match. Orlando will look to carry that defensive form against a Cincinnati side the club describes as dangerous in transition.
 Midfielder Braian Ojeda scored the only goal in the Decision Day win over New England, his second goal as a Lion, in a match that secured a home playoff game. The Paraguayan is known mainly for his work rate and defensive presence in midfield, and the goal showed another part of his game.
 Orlando City's playoff place marks the club's seventh straight postseason appearance, the longest active streak in MLS. The Lions first qualified in 2020.
 On individual milestones, Martín Ojeda (47) needs one assist to pass Mauricio Pereyra for the club record across all competitions, while Iván Angulo (45) needs two to tie Ojeda and Pereyra. Daryl Dike (22) is one goal from tying former Lion Dom Dwyer (23) for eighth on the club's all-time scoring chart.
